questions.q: Why not compare a prompt's conditioning directly with a latent?
options: They are in different spaces, so the cosine means nothing
questions.answer: They are in different spaces, so the cosine means nothing
questions.why: Scores need a pair of encoders trained together. The lab's rotation shows what happens without that.

questions.q: A CLIP cosine of 0.35 on an image. What can you conclude alone?
options: Little: compare it with other scores from the same model
questions.answer: Little: compare it with other scores from the same model
questions.why: Hessel et al. report a range of about 0 to 0.4. An absolute doesn't translate into a percent.

questions.q: A shorter caption scores higher than a fuller one on the same image. Why?
options: It asks for less, so less can be missing
questions.answer: It asks for less, so less can be missing
questions.why: The lab's 'red car' beats the full caption. A score isn't a count of what you asked for.

questions.q: Two renders tie on a five-item checklist. What should you read next?
questions.why: Both are 0.60 in the lab, with opposite failures.

questions.q: Why does a checklist mark count as a weak basis to pick the better sampler here?
options: It's one seed, marked by one reader
questions.answer: It's one seed, marked by one reader
questions.why: See CU-470: one seed can name either winner.
